title: Tommy Miles's band 1939-41: personnel and arrangements
summary: Phillips lists the 1939 band with Malachi, Chester Brown, Pete Jones and himself, with arrangements by Mundy, Hill and Jefferson, until it broke up in 1941.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who was in the band when you were there? And what was the band into? What kind of stuff did they play?
Same thing.
Phillips - 172
Who was in it when you were there?

It wasn't as big a band as... That band wasn't; it was a smaller band. Paul Jones and Harry Curtis, who was playing first alto. John Malachi on piano. Tommy on drums. Benny Fonville playing bass. Chester Brown was playing guitar. Good one, too; he died. Good guitar player, man. He was way ahead of his time. Chester Brown on guitar. And Pete Jones playing trombone. Reds McCurry was playing trumpet. And I was playing trumpet and Jefferson also. We had Pete Jones on trombone. And that was it. That was that band.
That was the '39 band.
Yeah.
What kind of stuff were they playing? What kind of solos and all that stuff? What was it like?

Same thing that the other band was playing. Playing the same arrangements -- Mundy's arrangements, Hill's arrangements. Playing the same arrangements. "Rhapsody In Blue" -- they had an arrangement on that. Things like that. They had some heavy arrangements. He had a hell of a good book, because he had Mundy's arrangements, Hill's arrangements, Jeff's arrangements. We had three helluva arrangers in the band, so that kept the band going, kept them up all the time.
When did that band break up?
Phillips - 173
How long were you with them?
You were there until the end?
Yes.
You were with them for three years.
Yeah, something like that. About two-and-a-half years.
How long was John in the band?
We all left about the same time.
